headline: Nike Founder Phil Knight Gives $1B to Public University
meta_description: Phil Knight donates $1 billion to University of Oregon, the largest single gift to a U.S. public university in history, enabling a new engineering college.
summary_short: Nike co-founder Phil Knight and his wife Penny have donated $1 billion to the University of Oregon, marking the largest single donation to a public university ever.
body:
Phil Knight, co-founder of Nike, has made a gift that will reshape higher education in Oregon. He and his wife Penny are donating $1 billion to the University of Oregon—the largest single donation to an American public university in history. The announcement came when Knight called university president Karl Scholz at a San Francisco airport terminal, catching him completely off guard. The timing is strategic: Oregon faces a shortage of engineers, and Knight's gift will allow the university to establish a full undergraduate engineering college, combining educational programs that were previously scattered across the institution.

Knight's connection to the university runs deep. He co-founded Nike alongside Bill Bowerman, his former track coach at Oregon, and has been giving back to his alma mater for decades. His name already graces the law center, sports complexes, and library across campus. The Knight Foundation had previously contributed $1 billion in combined gifts to the university, which some refer to as the "University of Nike." This new donation essentially doubles that legacy.

What makes this gift remarkable is both its scale and its timing. University leadership had been discussing plans for an engineering college with Knight for years, but nothing was scheduled for the day he called. The $1 billion commitment arrives as the institution was bracing for budget cuts—President Scholz had recently planned $65 million in reductions as out-of-state enrollment was expected to decline. Knight's words capture the larger vision: "To make an audacious dream a reality requires more than a vivid imagination. It also requires the sort of opportunity that our great American universities have historically provided. This is no time to abandon them." His investment suggests a powerful vote of confidence in public higher education.
